moodReason: Stocks fell for a seventh straight session, pushing the S&P 500 into a correction, and Nvidia dropped 14 percent after reports of an SEC accounting review. Hawkish Fed talk about more rate hikes adds to the pressure.

stories.headline: Nvidia plunges 14% after reports of an SEC accounting review
stories.what: Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia, and California's attorney general sent the company an investigative subpoena. Nvidia closed at $125.53, a 52-week low, and chip peers such as Micron and AMD fell more than 12%.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest driver of AI-related index weight, so a sharp drop in the leading chip name pulls down the whole AI trade and the indexes that hold it.

stories.headline: S&P 500 enters a correction as the AI selloff spreads
stories.what: The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39, down 3.70%, its seventh straight loss and an 8.6% drop for the week, its worst since April 2025. The Dow and S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record highs, and the VIX closed at 35.89, its first close above 30 since late March.
stories.why: Technology fell 7.27% and was the worst sector. Consumer staples were the only sector to finish higher, a sign of defensive rotation rather than a full exit from stocks. Taiwan's TAIEX fell 6.23%, a record weekly loss, which shows the chip selloff is global.

stories.headline: Fed hawks push for more rate hikes, and markets lean toward a December increase
stories.what: St. Louis Fed President Musalem said the US likely needs several rate hikes by spring to control inflation, and called the current 3.75% to 4.00% rate accommodative. Kalshi prediction markets priced a 25 basis point hike at the December meeting as the most likely outcome, though the snapshots they showed ranged from 77% to 91%.
stories.why: Higher expected rates raise borrowing costs and lower the value of future earnings, which weighs most on high-valuation growth stocks. A hike bet also removes the hope of a Fed rescue during the selloff.

stories.headline: Treasury yields fall sharply as investors buy safe assets
stories.what: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 12 basis points to 4.92%, and the 2-year fell 13 basis points to 4.63%. Bond prices rose as stocks sold off.
stories.why: Lower yields ease pressure on stock valuations. The move came from risk-off buying rather than a softer Fed, so it reads as a flight to safety, not a sign that rate hikes are off the table.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares fall in their first full trading session
stories.what: Anthropic (ANT) fell 8.50% to $88.91 in its first full session after its IPO. The stock is still above its $83 IPO price.
stories.why: A weak debut for one of the largest new AI listings adds to doubts about AI valuations at the same moment that Nvidia and other AI leaders are under pressure. It may also weigh on sentiment for future tech IPOs.

stories.headline: Global Payments jumps 10% on a reported takeover approach
stories.what: Bloomberg reported that private equity firm GTCR is exploring a takeover of Global Payments worth about $50 billion including debt. The stock rose 9.95% on the news.
stories.why: Buyout interest in a beaten-down company suggests some private buyers still see value in lower-priced stocks. It is a single-stock story, so its effect on the broader market is limited.

watch.item: US stock markets closed for Thanksgiving
December FOMC decision (date from a Kalshi listing, verify on the Fed calendar)
Any follow-up on the SEC accounting review of Nvidia

bottomLine: The AI and chip trade is driving a broad selloff, and the S&P 500 is now more than 10% below its record. Rising rate-hike expectations remove the usual hope of a Fed rescue, and a VIX above 35 signals real fear. Defensive stocks held up, so investors are rotating rather than leaving equities entirely. The next test is whether the Nvidia probe deepens and whether the selling steadies before the holiday-shortened week.
